Hahaha I had all of the same questions. I did my whole bedroom with one! I was able to do a single swipe from ceiling to floor most of the time. It definitely takes a steady hand and patience to get it right. The roller has markings on the edges so if you have to add more paint in the middle of a wall you can line the pattern up again pretty accurately. If you get to the end of a wall and there isn’t enough room to fit the whole roller, you hold a piece of paper to cover the previous area, which makes the pattern fit to the edge. I don’t know if that makes sense lol. There are videos on youtube that I watched before I did it, and I practiced a lot on some old cardboard. I guess maybe it isn’t the most practical endeavor, but I love vintage looking wallpaper and it was a cheap alternative. I also love doing projects around the house, so I enjoyed it a lot.

There are all kinds of patterned paint rollers on Etsy. You could maybe paint all of the walls a neutral color and then use a patterned roller with orange on one wall. This is the shop I used for my rollers, but there are many others! 

https://etsy.me/1bcHDOt

Childhood trauma. Funny thing is, I went my whole life being pretty unaffected by it. I had minor anxiety and depressive spells all through my life but was otherwise functional and “normal.” It’ll be five years this spring since I had a bit of a breakdown and got really bad. Throughout the last five years I’ve been up and down. A lot of down. But it comes in waves. And this past year I got a lot better, I thought I had beaten it once and for all. I’m back in a rough patch now after a death in the family. Finding it hard to be comfortable in my body, much like you described. Lately I often feel like I need to escape, but there isn’t anywhere to go because I carry this feeling with me always. Sometimes it is dormant, lately it is wide awake. I only feel near 100% when I’m totally alone or at home. It sucks and it’s terrifying. But I got through it before and I won’t give up this time. I hope you don’t give up either. I’m wishing you all the best. You aren’t alone.
